LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 1.3.1 GENDER NEUTRAL LANGUAGE

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.3: Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can one avoid gender bias in communication?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify gender biased words and phrases in oral and written texts
2. use gender neutral words and phrases in sentences

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GRAMMAR IN USE 1.3.1 GENDER NEUTRAL LANGUAGE
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GRAMMAR IN USE 1.3.1 GENDER NEUTRAL LANGUAGE
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify gender biased words and phrases in oral and written texts

What this means
In this part you learn to identify gender biased words and phrases in oral and written texts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify gender biased words and phrases in oral and written texts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify gender biased words and phrases in oral and written texts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use gender neutral words and phrases in sentences

What this means
In this part you learn to use gender neutral words and phrases in sentences. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use gender neutral words and phrases in sentences.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use gender neutral words and phrases in sentences. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify gender biased words and phrases in oral and written texts)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language to a partner. (skill: use gender neutral words and phrases in sentences)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify gender biased words and phrases in oral and written texts.
3. Practise this skill: use gender neutral words and phrases in sentences.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can one avoid gender bias in communication?
2. Which words demonstrate gender sensitivity in communication?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify gender biased words and phrases in oral and written texts.
5. Be able to: use gender neutral words and phrases in sentences.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
